description: From a bug report or a written contract, can a shipped coding agent make a change to nb, a .NET codebase of about 13,000 lines it cannot read whole? Five tasks report a defect planted in nb at a pinned revision and one asks for a feature; hidden acceptance says whether the change is right, and nb's own tests say whether anything else broke.

planted.about: what is planted in nb at the pinned revision; a stage belongs to the one it reports

far-cause.note: a defect whose symptom is in a different module from its cause

red-test.note: a defect one of nb's own tests catches

report-only.note: a defect no test catches, reported by a user

two-causes.note: two defects behind one report, the second showing once the first is fixed

assistant.about: the agent and the model that make the change

qwen.note: Qwen Code on the local model: the free shakedown

stages.about: A new feature across nb's tool surface, oracle, budget and transcript: a tool the model asks its user with, answered from the answer sheet, to a written contract
stages.prompt:
nb has no user. When a model needs something from one, all it can do today is end its turn with a question, and the oracle (an answer sheet attached to the program; see *On `oracle`* in `docs/conversation-program-cli.md`) judges that last message. I'd like the model to be able to ask through a tool as well. Please add it, to this contract:

1. A native tool named `ask_user_question`, with one required string argument, `question`.
2. The tool is offered to the model only while the program has an `oracle` sheet attached. `tools -ask_user_question` removes it like any other native tool, so the name has to be valid in a `tools` directive. With no oracle, a call to it is refused the way any unadvertised tool is.
3. A call is answered by the same oracle judgement an end-of-turn ask gets, with the question standing where the model's last message would. On a hit, the tool result is the selected sheet entries, verbatim, composed exactly as the end-of-turn answer is.
4. If the sheet has no answer (the judge's verdict is anything but entry ids), the tool result is exactly `The user has no answer to that question. Proceed on your own judgement.` and the run goes on. This does not end the run and does not set `oracle_miss`.
5. A hit counts against `budget oracle_turns`, the same counter end-of-turn resolutions use. A question that would be a hit when the budget is already spent gets the tool result `The user is no longer answering questions in this run.`, and the run then ends with exit reason `oracle_budget`.
6. In the transcript this is an ordinary `tool_call` and `tool_result`. The `tool_result` event also carries `"source": "oracle"`, and on a hit `"keys"`, the selected entry ids. The trailer's `oracle_turns` counts hits from either route.
7. The judge call's tokens count in the run's usage, as the end-of-turn judge call's do.
8. So that it can be tested: on the Mock provider, `MOCK:tool=ask_user_question <text>` sends `<text>` as the `question` argument, and a `MOCK:oracle=<verdict>` rider inside the question scripts the judge's verdict, as it does for an end-of-turn ask.

Nothing that works today should change, the end-of-turn oracle included. Add tests for the new behaviour and bring the docs up to date.

stages.about: A report of documented behaviour as a bug: the right outcome is no code change and an answer that says where the docs describe it
stages.prompt:
Bug: `@file` includes don't work in the middle of a prompt. With a program like

```
run @notes.md and summarise it
```

nb sends the literal text `@notes.md and summarise it` to the model; the file is never included. `run @notes.md` on its own line works fine, so the include code is clearly there. Can you fix this?

stages.about: A report that some transcripts replay as seeds with a message out of place; the defect is in a different module from the one that replays, and shows only for runs the report does not characterise
stages.prompt:
We keep the transcript of every nb run (`--output jsonl`) and often continue one the next day by replaying it as a seed (`--seed run.jsonl`) with a follow-up prompt. On some of them the model behaves oddly after the replay, as though it had been told off before it did anything. A colleague compared what was sent to the provider and says one user message sits earlier in the replayed conversation than it did in the original run. Most transcripts replay exactly; I haven't worked out what the bad ones have in common, and I can't share them.

nb's tests and evals all pass. Can you find what's wrong and fix it? Don't change the existing tests.

stages.about: One of nb's own tests is red; find the defect behind it and fix it without touching the tests
stages.prompt:
The build is red on main: `dotnet test` fails in nb.Tests. Find out why and fix it.

The unit tests are what to go by here; you don't need `evals/run.sh` for this one. Don't change the existing tests.

stages.about: A user's report that headings vanish from a multi-line prompt, with no failing test; reproduce it, find the defect and fix it
stages.prompt:
A user sent this in:

> My system prompt is Markdown, written over several lines with continuation backslashes. The model never sees my headings. This is the program:
>
> ```
> system You answer support mail for a bike shop. \
> # Rules \
> Never promise a refund. \
> # Tone \
> Be brief.
> run A customer asks whether they can return a helmet.
> ```
>
> `nb --compile` on it shows a system prompt with no `# Rules` and no `# Tone` line in it. I'm sure this used to work.

nb's tests all pass. Can you find what's wrong and fix it? Don't change the existing tests; add one if it helps.

stages.about: A user's report that apply_patch fails on the end of a CRLF file; two defects contribute, and the second shows only once the first is fixed

acceptance.description: the task's hidden acceptance passes: the reported defect is gone, or, for a report of documented behaviour, no code was changed

tests-green.description: nb's own tests pass on the changed repository (a failing run is repeated once, since one of nb's tests depends on timing)

planted-present.description: the repository the agent was given held this task's planted defect

tests-untouched.description: no test nb already had was edited or deleted

named-cause.description: the closing message names the file that holds the defect (for a report of documented behaviour, the page that documents it)
